para: The graph is generative, not merely archival. Its primary value is not as a fixed catalogue of known calculi but as a framework for producing calculi that have not previously been described. Every blank region — every part of the graph where the duality construction predicts a node but no independently named calculus exists — is a prediction: there ought to be a calculus there, with such-and-such properties, and the construction specifies in advance what its rules must look like. Some of these predictions will be confirmed by the rediscovery of calculi that have already been studied under other names; others will identify genuinely new systems. In either case the graph provides what the existing literature does not: a principled basis for asking What is missing? and a method for answering the question that is independent of historical accident.
